why: Repo pins PyTorch 0.4 (2018). PyPI no longer hosts it; only the CPU wheel resolves. GPU training on modern drivers is unverified. A human must choose: CPU-only on pinned versions, or adapt code to modern PyTorch - and decide whether adaptation is acceptable for a reproduction claim.

The paper never states total episodes or stopping rule. Repo defaults (10000 epochs, early-stop patience 200) are repo choices, not paper statements. A human must set the budget and record it in the run.
License reads NOASSERTION on GitHub. Needed at runtime (imported by train.py). Human/legal review required before redistribution or institutional deployment.
Official repo ships splits only; images derive from ILSVRC-2012 (research-only, non-commercial). Human must own the acquisition path and license call. Excluded from prototype scope.

No random seed anywhere; results are averages over 1000 (Omniglot) or 600 (miniImageNet) randomly generated episodes. A human must define what counts as close enough (e.g., within reported confidence intervals) - the AI only reports deltas.
By PaperLab hard rules, only a human (professor / lead researcher) may declare whether the run supports the paper's claims. The AI assembles evidence; the verdict field stays empty until signed.
